record.paper_title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
record.original_question: Does there exist a bounded set A⊂R^d for which no set S minimizes H1(S) among all sets such that S∪A is connected, showing that closedness of A may be necessary for solvability?

evidence.quote: Question 2.3. Is it possible to find a bounded set A⊂R^d such that the problem: “find S such that H1(S) is minimal among all sets for which S ∪ A is connected” does not have a solution?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\mathcal{H}^1$ denote the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (with $d \geq 2$). Given a set $A \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, consider the variational problem of finding a set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ that minimizes $\mathcal{H}^1(S)$ among all sets $S$ such that $S \cup A$ is connected. It is known that if $A$ is compact, a minimizer exists. Determine whether there exists a bounded (but not necessarily closed) set $A \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ for which this minimization problem admits no solution; equivalently, decide whether closedness of $A$ is necessary for solvability.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in a recent (2025) collection of open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers, attributed to E. Paolini. No resolution was found in the literature search.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
status_evidence.snippet: Question 2.3. Is it possible to find a bounded set A⊂R^d such that the problem ... does not have a solution?

status_evidence.title: On the Steiner tree connecting a fractal set
status_evidence.snippet: For compact A there exists a Steiner set; closedness/compactness assumptions are standard in existence results.
status_evidence.claim: Existence is known for compact A; the bounded non-closed case is unresolved.
